unit.title: Agents for teachers’ work, checked and approved

lesson.title: Check its work
lesson.subtitle: Check every call before it runs, with a few strict rules and a person’s yes

video.title: Check its work

Mr Joseph Mwangi — computer studies teacher, Kenya (cameo)

chapters.label: What to check in a call

scenes.visual: A list: Asked: tidy the library; Proposed: “tisums” the library; Who checks?.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: I asked our agent to remind me to tidy the library tomorrow at nine. It proposed a reminder to tisums the library. Tisums! If nobody had checked, that’s what I’d have got.

scenes.animation: The Darsi mark pops in; the title slides up.
scenes.narration: Today: checking an agent’s work before it counts.

scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.on_screen_text: Check the call, not just the answer
scenes.narration: An agent’s answer is the last thing you see. By then, the tool has already run. The moment to check is earlier: after the model writes a call, and before the app runs it.

scenes.visual: A list: The right tool?; From your words or a result?; The right shape?.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Check three things in every call. Is it the right tool? Did every name and number come from your words, or from a result? And does each detail have the right shape, like a time that exists?

scenes.visual: Code typed out on a card: timetable{"class":"9C","day":"tomorrow"} …
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Darsi Tiny’s real slips look like this. Asked about class nine Z, which doesn’t exist, it called the timetable for nine C. It copied a time of twenty-five o’clock as it was. And tidy became tisums.

scenes.visual: A list: Reviews each call before it runs; A few strict rules, in code; The rest goes to a person.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: A checker reviews each call before it runs. It doesn’t need to be clever: a few strict rules in code catch a model’s slips without guessing. What the rules can’t decide goes to a person.

scenes.visual: A list: The tool is on; Every detail has the right shape; Names from your words or a result; No failed step before it; A person said yes to any action.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: The team lab’s checker has five rules. The tool must be switched on. Every detail must have the right shape. Every name and number must come from your words or a result. No step before it may have failed. And any action needs a person’s yes.

scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Quick check! I asked about class nine Z, and the agent proposes the timetable for nine C. Which rule stops it?

scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Nine C isn’t in your request, or in any result. So the checker stops the call before anything runs, and hands it back to you. Then you ask again, in other words.

scenes.visual: A list: Every call, logged; What ran, what was stopped; Who said yes; The log answers questions.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Keep a record, too. A good agent app logs every call: what was asked, what ran, what was stopped, and who said yes. When a parent asks why a message went out, the log answers.

scenes.visual: A list: Darsi Tiny proposes each call; Weather: the checker passes it; Library and 9Z: stopped; Then switch the checker off.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.on_screen_text: App lab: a planner and a checker
scenes.narration: In the app, Darsi Tiny is the planner and proposes each call. Send the weather request: the checker passes it. Send the library reminder and nine Z: the checker stops them. Then switch the checker off.

scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Your turn. The checker passes a reminder for tomorrow at eight. Who should decide whether it’s set?

scenes.visual: Summary points: Check the call before it runs; A few strict rules, in code; A person gives the final yes.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.on_screen_text: Check the call before it runs · A few strict rules, in code · A person gives the final yes
scenes.narration: A person, because a reminder is an action. Remember: check the call before it runs. A few strict rules catch a model’s slips. And a person gives the final yes, with a record kept.

scenes.visual: A list: Play “Be the checker”; Cards with planted slips; Apply the five rules; Which slip was hardest?.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Try it in class tomorrow: play Be the checker. Give groups proposed calls on cards, some with planted slips. Groups apply the five rules and stop or pass each card. Which slip was hardest to spot?

checkpoints.prompt: You asked about class 9Z; the agent proposes the timetable for 9C. Which rule stops it?

options.text: Every name comes from your words or a result

checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — 9C is in neither your request nor any result, so the checker stops the call before the tool runs.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — the tool is on, and reading a timetable needs no yes. The slip is the name: 9C came from nowhere.

checkpoints.prompt: The checker passes a reminder for tomorrow at 8:00. Who should decide whether it is set?

options.text: The checker: it passed the rules
The model: it asked for it
A person: a reminder is an action

checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — the rules catch slips, but a reminder is an action, so a person gives the final yes.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — passing the rules isn’t the same as being wanted. Any action waits for a person’s yes.
